OCTOBER FIELD LOG — CAT HEAD AREA, LAKE MARION

This is a retrospective of our firsthand October fishing trips, not a claim that the same fish are holding there today. October's fishing gave us a documented starting point for evaluating the seasonal move into November.

OCTOBER 5 — Our trip produced approximately 240 pounds of catfish, including four fish over 50 pounds. Wind was reported around 7 mph from the north-northeast to north-northwest. These are trip totals, not a lakewide catch forecast.

OCTOBER 13 — Fishing near Cat Head, morning surface water temperature was about 75.7°F. Bait was observed in approximately 10–18 feet of water. The recorded catch included a 6-pound channel catfish and an 8-pound blue catfish, followed by a blue reported around 40 pounds later in the trip.

OCTOBER 21 — Near Cat Head, water temperature ranged from approximately 70.3°F to 72.8°F during the trip. We caught blue catfish weighing approximately 30 and 25 pounds in about 18 feet of water, and later a blue around 40 pounds in approximately 22 feet on an upslope.

WHAT THE LOG TELLS US — During the documented October outings, productive water included bait-related structure and depth changes in the upper-teen to low-20-foot range. The October 21 upslope catch shows why the relationship between contours can matter as much as any single depth. These results document where and how we fished on those dates; they do not establish a current bite at Cat Head or across Lake Marion.

NEXT STEP — November coverage will investigate a new location and compare its contours, bait, water conditions, sonar observations and actual fishing results against this October baseline. Public reports explain the general-area structure and reasoning; exact GPS positions and advanced tactics are available to Master Fisherman Patreon supporters.

DIVERSION CANAL FLOW ASSESSMENT — November 5, 2026 (11:42 a.m. EST audit)

STATUS: Current Diversion Canal discharge and current speed NOT independently verified. No direct, time-stamped canal-flow measurement was available in the sources checked. Do not interpret hydro generation schedules as canal flow measurements.

LATEST OPERATOR-PUBLISHED DAILY LAKE LEVELS: Santee Cooper's public lake-data feed, last updated November 4, reports November 3 Lake Marion 74.22 ft and Lake Moultrie 74.11 ft, a nominal 0.11-ft (about 1.3-inch) difference, with Marion higher. November 2 was 74.22 ft and 74.13 ft respectively, a nominal 0.09-ft difference. Thus the operator-reported difference widened 0.02 ft from November 2 to November 3, driven by a 0.02-ft decline at Moultrie while Marion remained unchanged. These are DAILY values, not simultaneous November 5 observations. The exact reference datum and measurement comparability of these two displayed values have not been independently reconciled against the individual USGS gauge metadata in this audit; treat the difference as provisional and do not use it to calculate canal velocity or discharge. No November 4 or November 5 operator daily elevation values were available in the verified feed at audit time.

TENTATIVE HYDRO SCHEDULE (operator page last updated November 4): Thursday November 5, Jefferies Hydro 2 p.m.–10 p.m.; St. Stephen Hydro not scheduled to run. Friday November 6, Jefferies noon–8 p.m.; St. Stephen not scheduled to run. These are planned windows, subject to change, NOT verified actual generation or canal discharge. The November 3 operator table reports Jefferies discharge 4,299 and St. Stephen discharge 54 (operator table units; these are facility-specific reported discharges, NOT Diversion Canal measurements). Do not assume St. Stephen's unscheduled status implies zero canal flow or that Jefferies operation proves a particular canal current.

DIRECTIONAL INTERPRETATION (INFERENCE ONLY): If both operator lake elevations use a comparable vertical reference and the positive Marion-to-Moultrie difference persists, movement from Lake Marion toward Lake Moultrie is hydraulically plausible. The dated, small elevation difference and changing downstream operations do not establish the actual November 5 direction at every point, current strength, or whether conditions are fishable. No qualitative strength classification is supported by an observed canal discharge or velocity. Verify locally before navigating or choosing current-dependent fishing presentations.

SOURCES CHECKED NOVEMBER 5: Santee Cooper public operational feed (dated November 4): https://azapp-lakespublic-prd-001.azurewebsites.net/ ; Santee Cooper explanation of lake-level management and hydro operations: https://www.santeecooper.com/community/lakes/lake-data/ ; official USGS station links for datum/time checks: Marion at Elloree https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02169921/ and Moultrie at Pinopolis https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02172000/ . Gauge metadata and latest synchronized observations were not independently retrieved in this audit. This assessment replaces the November 4 commentary.
level_analysis: Daily lake-level readings above are published with USGS station timestamps. Review each gauge's vertical datum before comparing Lake Marion and Lake Moultrie. Water movement and reservoir operations require separate verification; elevation alone cannot establish canal discharge.
